title: Conditional transfer to the full norm-topological algebraic closure for supported finite models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Omega\}$, with discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$, using all continuous maps, also for $\Omega$. On each scheme $V$, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Use the small sites and indexing universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].
Let $t:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume that for every locally torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, without a common annihilator, the actual restriction $H^q(T_{\mathrm{et}},F)\to H^q((T_0)_{\mathrm{et}},t_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}F)$ is bijective for every $q\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Choose a finite chain
$$S=T_r\xrightarrow{a_r}T_{r-1}\longrightarrow\cdots\xrightarrow{a_1}T_0'=T,$$
where each arrow is either a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $J_k=(a_k)_!$ in the open case and $J_k=(a_k)_*$ in the closed case, and put $J=J_1\circ\cdots\circ J_r$, with $J=\mathrm{id}$ for $r=0$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. The symbol $T_0'$ is only the root of this chain; the closed member of the pair is $T_0$.
For any coefficient ring $R$ mentioned below, its sheaf is $R_V=p_V^*C(-,R)$; a finite scalar local model means a module locally isomorphic to $R_V\otimes_{\underline{R}}\underline P$ for a finitely presented scalar $R$-module $P$, on a pro-étale cover. Define $\mathsf B_R(t)$ to mean: for every finite chain of the specified open and closed immersions ending in $T$, and every finite scalar local model $L$ on its source, the actual ordinary module-derived restriction
$$\rho_{R,J,L}:R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},J L[0])\longrightarrow R\Gamma((T_0)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},t^*J L[0])$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. This notation is just the displayed quantified property, not an additional definition node. It includes all chains, including the identity chain, with no quasi-compactness assumption on the complement of $t$.
Assume additionally that $\mathsf B_{E'}(t)$ holds for every finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E'\subseteq\Omega$, with its norm topology. Then $\mathsf B_\Omega(t)$ holds for the condensed ring $P\mapsto C(P,\Omega)$ formed using all continuous maps into the incomplete norm-topological field $\Omega$. The conclusion includes finite scalar local models whose transition maps have not been given over a common finite $E'$. It concerns the actual restriction in the uncompleted ambient category. It does not assert $C(-,\Omega)=\varinjlim_{E'} C(-,E')$, or any finite-field-of-definition theorem, or comparison for images of arbitrary maps of local models. The original torsion-rigidity hypothesis is retained. No properness, regularity or Noetherianity, invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes, or replacement by the completed field $\mathbf C_\ell$ is imposed.

proof.text: Fix a support chain $J$ and finite scalar $\Omega$-local model $L$. The derived-generation theorem applies to this exact all-continuous coefficient ring on the qcqs root $T$: it puts $JL[0]$ in its explicitly defined class $\mathscr G_T$. We will prove that every object of that class has invertible actual restriction. Its generators are $J'_B(B_W\otimes_{E_W}N)[0]$, with arbitrary allowed support chain $J'$, finite intermediate field $E$ and finite locally free $E_W$-module $N$. Such $N$ is an allowed finite scalar local model. No finite-field model for $L$ or its transition maps is chosen.

proof.text: We may compute all following section comparisons after scalar restriction to a fixed finite $E$. Internal/sectionwise transport preserves underlying sheaves, sections and the open/closed functors, including their units and counits. Exact inverse image for any pulled-back condensed coefficient has the same underlying abelian inverse image; hence it commutes with scalar restriction. The unit-normalized derived-section isomorphisms for scalar restriction identify the actual derived restriction maps as well: choose a coefficient-module K-injective resolution $I$ and a resolution of $t^*I$, and compare their scalar restrictions to K-injective resolutions over $E$. Both routes from the original module to the target resolution lift the identical underived section unit. The K-injective comparison principle makes the two routes equal after localization. This uses comparison resolutions over $E$, rather than assuming the forgotten complexes or $t^*I$ are K-injective. Therefore it suffices to test invertibility over $E$ with these canonical section identifications.

proof.text: Fix one generating chain $J'$ with source $W$, finite field $E$, and lisse $E_W$-module $N$. Use $C$ for the finite-subextension-valued ring and $B$ for all norm-continuous functions. For finite $F\supseteq E$ put $H_F=J'_E\operatorname{Res}_{E_W\to F_W}(F_W\otimes_{E_W}N)$. Each $F_W$-extension of $N$ is locally finite free, so the hypothesis $\mathsf B_F(t)$ applies to this same chain. Step 2 identifies its actual restriction with $\rho_{H_F}$. The tail coefficient-colimit theorem gives $C_W=\varinjlim_{F\supseteq E}F_W$ over the small directed tail. Relative tensor preserves this colimit by its adjunction. Open extension preserves it as a left adjoint; closed pushforward preserves it because each target is qcqs and its open complement is quasi-compact. Inducting through $J'$ gives $H_C=\varinjlim_F H_F$, as $E_T$-module sheaves, with the actual scalar-inclusion maps. Here $H_C$ is precisely the first term of the topology-defect lemma. This colimit statement is about $C$, not $B$.

proof.text: Apply the closed-restriction continuity theorem over the coefficient ring $E$ to the strict diagram $H_F[0]$, which has common termwise lower bound zero. It identifies the restriction of $H_C[0]$ with the filtered colimit of the restriction arrows for $H_F[0]$. Each is invertible by step 3 and $\mathsf B_F(t)$; its filtered colimit is invertible, the colimit of the inverse arrows being its inverse. Thus $\rho_{H_C[0]}$ is invertible. The theorem applies to qcqs $T,T_0$ and needs no quasi-compactness of the complement of the original $t$.

proof.text: Let $m:H_C\to H_B$ and $D_{J',E,N}=[H_C\xrightarrow m H_B]$ in degrees $-1,0$ be exactly the objects of the topology-defect lemma for this generating chain. The pair satisfies that lemma's torsion hypothesis verbatim. It makes $\rho_D$ invertible without the comparison property $\mathsf B_E(t)$ as an extra premise. The mapping-cone triangle $H_C[0]\to H_B[0]\to D\to H_C[1]$ is distinguished. The closed-restriction theorem sends this triangle to a morphism of distinguished triangles, including its connecting arrow. Its first and third arrows are invertible by step 4 and the defect lemma, so the triangle isomorphism criterion makes its middle arrow $\rho_{H_B[0]}$ invertible. Step 2 transports this actual map to the $B$-module restriction for $J'_B(B_W\otimes_{E_W}N)[0]$, as required for this generator.

proof.text: Let $\mathscr R$ be the full replete class of $K$ for which the actual $\rho_K$ is invertible. It contains zero since the two additive section functors send zero to zero, and contains every generator by step 5. The closed-restriction theorem makes it shift-closed. For a distinguished triangle, its actual restrictions form a morphism of distinguished triangles; two-out-of-three makes it extension-closed. For a retract $K\xrightarrow{i}M\xrightarrow{p}K$ with $\rho_M$ invertible, the inverse of $\rho_K$ is $\Phi(p)\rho_M^{-1}\Psi(i)$: naturality and $pi=1$ make both composites identities. For a small product the theorem identifies its restriction with the product of the restrictions, whose inverse is the product of their inverses. For a strict small filtered diagram with a common termwise lower bound, the theorem identifies restriction at the termwise colimit with the colimit of the restriction arrows; the colimit of their inverses is an inverse. Thus $\mathscr R$ satisfies every defining condition of $\mathscr G_T$, so the intersection defining $\mathscr G_T$ lies in $\mathscr R$. Step 1 now gives invertibility for $JL[0]$. The chain and model were arbitrary, proving $\mathsf B_\Omega(t)$, including zero models, empty schemes and identity chains.
